channel.title: Chovy's Blog
channel.description: Tech, agentic coding, and whatever else I'm building. By Anthony "chovy" Ettinger.

item.title: AI has finally enabled us CLI commandos
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Forty years after playing hangman on an IBM mainframe, the terminal is the interface again. AI agents run commands, and the people who never left the shell are the ones ready for it.

item.title: Post once, everywhere: myna now writes to your blogs and runs an ad for each post
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: myna 0.6.0 posts to Git and HTML blogs and opens a CrawlProof ad campaign for every post it publishes, so a launch is one command.

item.title: If all your traffic is bots, sell to the bots
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: A training crawler is a customer with a budget. Put the offer where a program will find it: robots.txt, a 402 with an x402 offer, a sales page at /crawl. @profullstack/x402-gateway does that in one middleware, it is on 38 sites, and tonight the first dollar cleared.

item.title: NicheDB: sources in, feeds out
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Live sports, TV releases and RSS all share one property: a big seed that grows every day from data that is already public. NicheDB is the platform version of that idea. Thirteen niches, 29 adapters, enrichment, and every row reachable by web, RSS, API, CLI and MCP.

item.title: Red Bull took my eye
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Pre-diabetic, then six months of a Red Bull every day, then type 2 diabetes, then a third cranial nerve palsy that shut my left eye. Red Bull was the last straw, not the cause. What I ignored, what is in the can, and why it is a drink for 20 year olds.

item.title: The 80,000 visitors a day were one crawler
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: One day, written up: the traffic on genrewatch was Meta's training crawler, so six sites now sell training bots a one dollar day pass over x402, a residential proxy fleet that no IP block can touch, a Next 16 proxy file that never ran, and why a headless browser does not fix the feed reader.

item.title: The $875 proxy bill was a 1.5 MB manifest
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: One day, written up: a proxy bill that looked like a credential leak and was really a playlist file polled every few seconds, SiriusXM landing on tipoffwatch, Spotify Connect on bittorrented.com, and a librespot bug where songs skipped after a few seconds.

item.title: A one-field funnel for launch.anapp.now
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: How the launch.anapp.now campaign site is built: one textarea instead of a signup form, a server-side handoff into Chovy that keeps the idea out of URLs, four hero headlines under test, and first-party tracking with no pixels.

item.title: One terminal window, 26 social networks
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: myna is a social media manager that runs in your terminal. It counts characters the way each network counts them, is honest about which of the 26 need a password and which need a browser, and keeps your credentials encrypted on your own machine.

item.title: Work is not disappearing. The job is.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: The salaried, 9-to-5, one-employer-for-decades package is an industrial-age artifact, and it is coming apart. What the return-to-office data, the independent workforce numbers and Harvard's research on degree requirements actually show.
